title: MccB-catalyzed C-terminal Thioesterification for Protein Bioconjugation
author: Yang, Weeks
materials: 0.5‐mL See Zeba Spin Desalting Column, 7K MWCO
LC‐MS system suitable for intact protein analysis

steps.title: Assess stepwise ligation suitability
steps.instruction: Determine if the target protein thioester should be isolated and ligated to an N‑terminal Cys peptide separately, e.g., when multiple peptide variants are needed or high organic solvent is required.

steps.title: Express and purify His‑MccB
steps.instruction: Produce His‑tagged E. coli MccB in BL21(DE3) cells under a T7 promoter, induce expression with IPTG, and purify the enzyme by Ni‑NTA affinity chromatography.

substeps.instruction: Transform BL21(DE3) cells with a plasmid encoding an N‑terminal His6 tag, TEV protease cleavage site, and MccB under a T7 promoter
Grow the transformed culture (typically 1 L) to the appropriate density
Induce protein expression with isopropyl β‑D‑1‑thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG)
Harvest cells and lyse the culture
Bind the clarified lysate to Ni‑NTA resin
Wash the resin and elute His‑MccB
Confirm purity (>95 %) and yield (>10 mg per 1 L culture)

steps.title: Generate thioester and ligate peptide
steps.instruction: Use the purified MccB to catalyze C‑terminal thioester formation on the target protein, isolate the thioester, and perform native chemical ligation with an N‑terminal Cys peptide, achieving near‑quantitative conversion to the protein–peptide conjugate.
